Hour 2 opens with Trent Conner's fantasy five, then NFL Week 10: Thursday in New Jersey, the Week 9 rewind, the full board, Steelers-Bengals for first place, implied team totals and locks.

blocks.title: Block 1: Last Saturday, the New Poll and the Second CFP Rankings

items.h: Notre Dame 31, No. 1 Miami 24
items.t: The game we previewed off the top of the show last week, and the road underdog won. Miami is out of the top spot in both polls for the first time all season - and Notre Dame, told on national television that it had no signature win, now has one.

items.h: Oregon 41, Ohio State 28
items.t: Ohio State fell TEN spots in the AP, 11 to 21, on top of the nine it fell the week before. Oregon came off the fringe back into the poll at No. 18.

items.h: Tennessee 34, No. 6 Kentucky 6
items.t: A 28-point beating of a top-10 team. The quietest 7-1 team in the country is now 7-2 and 13th.

items.h: Georgia 42, No. 10 Ole Miss 7, in Oxford
items.t: Georgia took No. 1 in both polls off it. Ole Miss fell seven.

items.h: Utah 28, No. 9 BYU 20 in the Holy War
items.t: Utah is 9-0 and one of the last two unbeaten teams in FBS.

items.h: Alabama 31, No. 14 LSU 13 and Texas 34, No. 18 Missouri 20
items.t: LSU fell nine spots. Missouri fell out of the AP poll entirely - and the committee still ranks it 22nd.

items.h: Oklahoma 23, No. 24 Florida 7
items.t: The unranked result with teeth. Florida dropped out of both polls.

items.h: The rest of the board
items.t: UCLA 34, Minnesota 20 (UCLA is 9-0). Texas Tech 53, West Virginia 48. Arizona 29, TCU 28 by a point - single-sourced, see the verify list. Houston 31, Cincinnati 24. Boise State 64, Colorado State 38. South Carolina 17, Texas A&M 9. Iowa 24, Northwestern 10. Wake Forest 77, Merrimack 0.

items.h: Indiana and USC were both idle
items.t: They play each other today. That is the game of the day - see Topic 6.

items.h: Two unbeaten teams left in all of FBS, and the AP has them second and fourth
items.t: 1 Georgia (8-1) with 53 first-place votes, 2 Utah (9-0) with 12, 3 Notre Dame (8-1) with 5, 4 UCLA (9-0), 5 Miami (8-1), 6 Indiana (8-1), 7 Alabama (7-2), 8 Texas (7-2), 9 Tennessee (7-2), 10 Texas Tech (8-1).

items.h: 11 through 25
items.t: Wake Forest, BYU, Kentucky, Houston, USC, Iowa, Boise State, Oregon, Ole Miss, South Carolina, Ohio State, Arizona, New Mexico, LSU, SMU.

items.h: The movement
items.t: Down: Ohio State minus 10, LSU minus 9, Ole Miss minus 7, Kentucky and BYU minus 5 each, Miami 1 to 5. Up: Iowa plus 5. Back in: Oregon at 18 and SMU at 25. Out: Missouri and Florida.

items.h: The vote math is the argument
items.t: 53 and 12 and 5 is a full 70-ballot panel - which means a 9-0 Utah has twelve first-place votes while a one-loss Georgia has fifty-three. Voters versus resume, out loud.

items.h: Others receiving votes
items.t: Missouri 50, Duke 49, Oklahoma State 21, Liberty 14, Louisville 10, North Texas 2.

segments.title: Topic 3. The second CFP rankings, out Tuesday

items.h: The CFP top 12
items.t: 1 Georgia, 2 Utah, 3 ALABAMA, 4 UCLA, 5 Notre Dame, 6 Texas, 7 Miami, 8 Tennessee, 9 Indiana, 10 BYU, 11 Kentucky, 12 Texas Tech.

items.h: 13 through 25
items.t: Wake Forest, Houston, Iowa, Oregon, South Carolina, USC, Ole Miss, Ohio State, LSU, Missouri, Arizona, Boise State, Oklahoma State. Florida dropped out from 24.

items.h: Fight one: Alabama is third with the committee and seventh in the AP
items.t: A two-loss team, four spots higher with the committee than with the voters, and ahead of a 9-0 UCLA.

items.h: Fight two: Boise State is 24th with the committee and 17th in the AP
items.t: Seven spots the other way - and it is the only team on the board in line for an automatic bid.

items.h: Fight three: the committee ranks two teams the AP doesn't, and skips two the AP does
items.t: Missouri is CFP 22 and AP unranked; Oklahoma State is CFP 25 and AP unranked. Meanwhile New Mexico is 8-1 and 23rd in the AP with no CFP ranking at all, and neither is SMU.

items.h: Fight four: Indiana is 8-1 and ninth, behind three two-loss teams
items.t: Chair Hunter Yurachek, Tuesday: 'Indiana was probably the victim of having a bye week at the wrong time.' A committee chair saying out loud that not playing cost a team. Attribute it as 'the committee chair said Tuesday.'

items.h: Handle this one carefully
items.t: CBS has Yurachek saying Notre Dame 'looked like the Notre Dame team that should be ranked No. 5.' Single-sourced. If you use it, say CBS reported it.

blocks.title: Block 2: West Virginia - the One That Got Away, and Kansas Tonight

items.h: Texas Tech 53, West Virginia 48 - no bowl eligibility yet
items.t: The Mountaineers are 5-4, 2-4 in the Big 12. Texas Tech scored 12 in the fourth quarter and came from seven down.

items.h: The two numbers that tell it
items.t: The teams combined for 1,220 total yards and 894 OF THEM CAME BEFORE HALFTIME. West Virginia's final five possessions netted MINUS FIVE YARDS, and the defense gave up 638.

items.h: Thomas Castellanos had a career night
items.t: Five touchdown passes, 18-of-27 for 362 with 102 rushing, and the go-ahead throw to Kenny Johnson with 2:44 left. J'Koby Williams ran for 160 with a 75-yard score.

items.h: Michael Hawkins Jr. has 19 rushing touchdowns, most in the country
items.t: 303 passing, 88 rushing and three rushing scores. wvusports calls 19 a school record, ESPN says he tied it - safest on air is '19, most in the nation.'

items.h: Cam Cook is West Virginia's first 1,000-yard rusher since Leddie Brown in 2021
items.t: 149 on 23 carries, 1,072 for the season.

items.h: Taron Francis caught three balls for 169 yards after catching zero all season
items.t: Including a 73-yard touchdown.

items.h: Rodriguez afterward
items.t: 'You got to play better, coach better to win. I mean, the defense was gross, first half.' And: 'It's ridiculous. I've never, in all my years of coaching, I can't ever remember it being this way.' And: 'So the answer is just play better defense. Play better defense. Got to play better defense.' The 'gross' line is also in the ESPN recap, so it is double-sourced.

items.h: The number that explains the season
items.t: West Virginia's offense is 10th in FBS in total yards. Its defense is 137th.

segments.title: Topic 5. Kansas at West Virginia tonight, 5:30 ET, ESPNU

items.h: Six wins is still on the table, and this is the best chance left
items.t: Kansas is 3-6, 1-5 in the Big 12, off a 33-32 loss to UCF. West Virginia is 5-4. Milan Puskar Stadium, 5:30 ET on ESPNU.

items.h: The number: West Virginia by about a field goal, total 64.5
items.t: DraftKings opened WVU -2.5 on Nov 8; the AP preview says 3. Two of the worst defenses in the league and the market says so. CBS's Week 11 odds article does not carry the game.

items.h: Against the spread and turnovers
items.t: West Virginia 5-3-1 ATS, Kansas 1-6-1. Turnover margin: WVU plus 2, Kansas minus 5.

items.h: West Virginia is out six
items.t: RB Andre Devine, TE Cam Ball, OL Amare 'Bubba' Grayson, OL Lamarcus Dillard, DL Darius Wiley and Emory Snyder. Josh Aisosa goes into the starting line for Grayson. Safety Matt Sieg has been CLEARED and is off the report; Da'Mare Williams is probable.

items.h: Kansas is out five, and one of them matters
items.t: Starting left guard CONNOR STROH, six-seven and 350, one of their best run blockers, replaced by junior Amir Herring. Also out: Jalen Dupree, Jack Utz, Kasen Carpenter, Grady Seyfert. QUARTERBACK COLE BALLARD IS QUESTIONABLE.

items.h: The people
items.t: Hawkins 1,901 passing, 12 TD, 2 INT plus the 19 on the ground. Cook 1,072 and 8. D.J. Epps 564 and 5. Kansas: Isaiah Marshall 1,716 with 11 and 7, Dylan Edwards 596 and 5, Nik McMillan 497 and 5.

items.h: Why tonight is the game
items.t: Houston at home next Saturday, time and TV still TBA - 14th in both polls - then at 9-0 Utah on FRIDAY NIGHT Nov 27 at 9:00 on FOX. Miss tonight and they have to get it off a top-15 team.

segments.title: Topic 6. Indiana-USC is the game, and four more ranked-vs-ranked

items.h: All college numbers below are DraftKings OPENERS from Nov 8
items.t: Say 'opened at,' not 'is.' They are five days old.

items.h: No. 15 USC at No. 6 Indiana, 3:30 on CBS - Indiana opened -7.5, total 49.5
items.t: CFP No. 18 at CFP No. 9, both off byes. This is the cleanest double-confirmation on the board - CBS's own line matches DraftKings exactly - and it is where Indiana answers the committee. USC is the team that beat Ohio State and saved Lincoln Riley's job.

items.h: No. 10 Texas Tech at Oklahoma State, 9:30 on ESPN - Oklahoma State opened -3, total 72.5
items.t: A TOP-12 TEAM IS A ROAD UNDERDOG, three books agree on the side, and that 72.5 is the highest number of the day by a distance. Oklahoma State is the committee's No. 25 and unranked in the AP.

items.h: No. 8 Texas at No. 24 LSU, 7:30 on ABC - LSU opened -4, total 46.5
items.t: CBS has -4.5 and 45.5. CFP No. 6 going to a CFP No. 21 that just lost by 18.

items.h: No. 2 Utah at No. 22 Arizona, 7:30 on FOX - Utah opened -3, total 53.5
items.t: The No. 2 team in both polls, 9-0, is a field-goal favorite on the road. CBS says 2.5. Arizona won by a point last week. Best pure upset spot on the board.

items.h: No. 11 Wake Forest at No. 25 SMU, noon on ESPN - no number
items.t: The sources do not agree on who is favored. Total is around 61.5. Talk about the game, do not quote a spread.

segments.title: Topic 7. Ranked teams on the road, and the rest of the board

items.h: Six more ranked teams travel
items.t: No. 7 Alabama at Vanderbilt 12:45 SECN, opened -19.5/54.5 - and Alabama is THIRD with the committee. No. 9 Tennessee at Texas A&M 3:00 ESPN, opened -3.5 (CBS says 2.5), total 41.5, lowest among the marquee games. Missouri at No. 1 Georgia 3:30 ABC, Georgia -14/47.5. Michigan at No. 18 Oregon 3:30 FS1, Oregon -10.5/40.5. No. 19 Ole Miss at Oklahoma 4:15 SECN, -2.5/50.5. No. 20 South Carolina at Arkansas 7:45 SECN, -8.5/51.5.

items.h: Two cautions in that group
items.t: Whether Missouri-Georgia is a ranked matchup depends entirely on which poll you read - CFP 22 versus AP unranked. And CBS contradicts ITSELF on Oregon at -11.5 and -8.5, so do not use a CBS number there.

items.h: Ranked teams at home outside the marquee
items.t: Duke at No. 5 Miami noon ABC, -14.5/54.5 - Miami's first game after losing the top ranking. Northwestern at No. 21 Ohio State noon FOX, -10.5/47.5. Baylor at No. 12 BYU 3:30 FOX, -7/48.5. Boston College at No. 3 Notre Dame 3:30 NBC, -31.5/52.5. Florida at No. 13 Kentucky 6:15 ESPN, -2.5/53.5 - two teams that got embarrassed last week. Oregon State at No. 17 Boise State 6:00 USA, -8.5/63.5. Purdue at No. 16 Iowa 7:30 NBC, -16.5/45.5. UNLV at No. 23 New Mexico 7:30 The CW, -13.5. Minnesota at Penn State 7:00 FS1, -7.5/43.5.

segments.title: Topic 8. The Heisman and the carousel

items.h: Do not name one Heisman favorite this morning
items.t: DraftKings on Nov 5, BEFORE Week 10, had Jeremiah Smith +150, Darian Mensah +170, CJ Carr +500, Trinidad Chambliss +1000 - now stale in both directions, because Smith's Ohio State and Mensah's Miami both lost.

items.h: The freshest board has CJ Carr in front
items.t: VegasInsider's multi-book table, odds as of Nov 12, is headlined 'Notre Dame's Carr Takes Over As Favorite' - bet365 +180, Caesars +160, with Smith +250/+240 and Mensah +240/+280. Say multi-book, not one price.

items.h: The carousel finally moved: NC State and Philip Rivers
items.t: ESPN's Schlabach and Thamel reported Wednesday night that Rivers, 44, is set to be the head coach with the board expected to finalize the contract Friday. He has NEVER COACHED IN COLLEGE - six seasons at St. Michael Catholic High School in Fairhope, Alabama, and he asked to finish that season, which ended Friday. His son Gunner committed in February. Russell Wilson was also in the discussions. No terms reported.

items.h: The other four openings are still open, three weeks in
items.t: Maryland (Locksley, Oct 21), Baylor (Aranda, Oct 25), Sam Houston (Longo, Oct 28), Florida State (Norvell, Nov 1). Florida State plays tonight at Pitt with no head coach.

items.h: If somebody raises Rodriguez
items.t: He is on no hot-seat list. 5-3 became 5-4, bowl eligibility is tonight, and the defense is 137th.

items.h: One college play and one sentence from each panelist
items.t: Name the book and the number you are taking - and if it is a college number, say 'opened at,' because these are Nov 8 openers.

items.h: The framing
items.t: The No. 2 team in the country is a three-point road favorite and a top-12 team is a road dog. Two chances to be a hero and two chances to look silly.

items.h: Tease
items.t: Trent at the top of the hour, and the Munich kickoff at 9:30 in the morning.

hours.title: Hour 2
hours.subtitle: Trent Conner's fantasy five at the top, then NFL Week 10 (9:00-10:00)

items.h: Lead with the quarterback carousel - six changes and one still unresolved
items.t: Kirk Cousins was traded from Las Vegas to Minnesota and is EXPECTED to start at Green Bay (first-team reps, not announced; Murray out with the hamstring). Carson Beck makes his first NFL start for Arizona with Minshew on IR. Kyle McCord starts in Miami with Malik Willis on IR. Deshaun Watson is reported back in Cleveland. Jacoby Brissett makes his first Ravens start Monday.

items.h: Las Vegas hands the offense to Fernando Mendoza, the No. 1 overall pick
items.t: Which makes Tre Tucker a sit: Seattle allows the fewest fantasy points to receivers in the league and only four wideouts have hit double digits against them all season.

items.h: The headline add: Corey Kiner, New England
items.t: TreVeyon Henderson is officially OUT, Rhamondre Stevenson did not practice Wednesday and is expected to miss weeks, and Kiner went 8 for 55 and a score on 4.9 a carry for the season. Ownership is 38.6 percent on ESPN and FOUR PERCENT on Yahoo - that gap is the whole tip, so name the platform. And Munich kicks at 9:30 Sunday morning, so there is no Sunday window to react.

items.h: Audric Estime took over the New Orleans backfield
items.t: 15 carries, 72 and a touchdown on a 47 percent snap share, 35 snaps to Kamara's 37, and Carolina gives up the second-most fantasy points to backs. He went from 9 percent to 48 percent owned on ESPN in three days. Risk: Travis Etienne started his activation window Wednesday.

items.h: Three cheap ones
items.t: KALEB JOHNSON, Green Bay - 14 for 68 and a score, 12 percent ESPN and ONE percent Yahoo, with Jacobs needing finger surgery. JORDAN WATKINS, San Francisco - led the 49ers in snaps, routes AND receiving yards in Week 9 at two percent owned. BREVYN SPANN-FORD, Dallas tight end, zero percent Yahoo, ran a route on 68.5 percent of dropbacks without Jake Ferguson and was targeted on 19 percent of them.

items.h: Stash list, graduating
items.t: Devin Singletary - 92 percent of snaps, 24 of 27 back opportunities (check Thursday's box score; Cam Skattebo came off the injury report). Dylan Sampson, who out-snapped Quinshon Judkins 47-25 with 26 routes - he is the passing-down back now, not a stash. Tyler Allgeier, who played 51 OF 53 SNAPS. Jordyn Tyson, on trajectory rather than production.

items.h: Still stashes
items.t: Jonah Coleman at 82 percent of Denver's snaps - but DENVER IS ON BYE, so he cannot help you this week. Kaelon Black. Antonio Williams at an 81 percent route share. Chris Rodriguez Jr. only while Tuten is out, and note six of his twelve opportunities last week were fourth-quarter garbage time.

items.h: Three reversals - say we are changing the call
items.t: MarShawn Lloyd is off the injury report and back in the Green Bay mix. Zach Charbonnet is not a stash at all, he is a START. And Omar Cooper Jr. holds at a 78 percent snap share.

items.h: Fading, and the biggest reversal of the week
items.t: MIKE WASHINGTON JR. was the No. 1 waiver priority in the country last week and played FIFTEEN SNAPS with three routes while Ashton Jeanty ran 23. He is a handcuff now. Also fading: Greg Dulcich (two catches for 14, and the McCord change hurts) and Ja'Kobi Lane (zero targets on 14 routes). DROP Brian Robinson Jr., who is on IR, and Dameon Pierce, who is season-ending.

items.h: One start, one sit, one stream, then out
items.t: START Zach Charbonnet at Las Vegas - the Raiders allow the most rushing yards per game and the highest yards per carry to backs, and only Atlanta has allowed more PPR points to the position over the last month. SIT Tony Pollard against Jacksonville, which allows 3.6 a carry and has given up FIVE total running back touchdowns in eight games. STREAM Indianapolis against Miami at one percent Yahoo and six percent ESPN, or Baltimore against the 0-8 Chargers, who lead the league in giveaways and score the fewest points in football.

items.h: Items Trent should check Saturday morning
items.t: The entire Friday injury report, which had not posted. The Minnesota quarterback. Green Bay's IR call on Jacobs. Rhamondre Stevenson. A.J. Brown, limited both days and traveling to Munich - FantasyPros calls it a coin flip. T.J. Hockenson did not practice Wednesday OR Thursday and CBS's Dave Richard still lists him a start, which is exactly the pattern that cost people Week 9. And check which team Pat Bryant plays for - ESPN has him on Carolina, Yahoo has him on Denver, and if it is Denver he is on a bye.

items.h: Washington won in New Jersey as a road underdog
items.t: DraftKings had the Giants -2.5 with a 40.5 total. The game went over at 45.

items.h: Jayden Daniels threw three touchdowns and his first two interceptions of the season in the same game
items.t: 23-of-33 for 249, with the winner 32 yards to STEFON DIGGS with 57 SECONDS LEFT - and picks to Jevon Holland and Ar'Darius Washington. That is the game in one line.

items.h: J.J. McCarthy threw for a career-high 293 in his first home start
items.t: 23-of-36, including a 66-yard go-ahead touchdown to Isaiah Likely in the fourth. Then Rasul Douglas intercepted him in the final minute to end it.

items.h: Diggs' 80th career receiving touchdown
items.t: Six catches on ten targets, 83 yards, and the 30th player in league history to reach 80.

items.h: Dominic Zvada missed a 33-yarder wide left
items.t: He is 8-of-14 since opening his career 9-for-9.

items.h: Injuries out of it
items.t: Washington tight end Chig Okonkwo left in the second quarter and returned; GIANTS SAFETY JASON PINNOCK left early in the third and did not.

items.h: The structural piece
items.t: Washington swept the series and now holds the head-to-head tiebreaker over a team it had TIED earlier this year. Giants 5-3-1, Commanders 3-5-1 - the only two teams carrying a tie, and they tied each other.

items.h: Bills 23, Vikings 6 on Monday night
items.t: Buffalo is 7-1 with the best record in the AFC. James Cook 107 on 31 carries, and BUFFALO HELD THE BALL 42 MINUTES AND 32 SECONDS. Minnesota ran for 51 yards; Justin Jefferson caught three of eleven targets.

items.h: Texans 44, Chargers 22 - and the Chargers are 0-8
items.t: C.J. Stroud 384 and five touchdowns. JUSTIN HERBERT WAS SACKED A CAREER-HIGH EIGHT TIMES, and Los Angeles had gone 37 STRAIGHT OFFENSIVE DRIVES WITHOUT A TOUCHDOWN.

items.h: Giants 19, Eagles 11
items.t: New York's first win in Philadelphia since 2013. Philadelphia has lost SEVEN STRAIGHT and is 2-7. Rookie Arvell Reese had 12 tackles, three sacks and a forced fumble - and 13 more tackles Thursday night.

items.h: Bears 27, Buccaneers 24 on a walk-off field goal
items.t: Cairo Santos from 38 as time expired - and Chicago won it while CALEB WILLIAMS THREW FOUR INTERCEPTIONS. They are 7-2 and on bye.

items.h: Broncos 26, Panthers 21
items.t: Denver is 7-2 and EXTENDED ITS NFL-RECORD STREAK TO SIXTEEN STRAIGHT WINS IN ONE-SCORE GAMES, finished by a Devon Key end-zone interception upheld on challenge.

items.h: Saints 23, Browns 22 in overtime - the one that moved a quarterback room
items.t: SHEDEUR SANDERS, starting for a concussed Deshaun Watson, went 19-of-31 for 297 and two scores including a 39-yard walk-off in overtime - and the two-point try to win it fell incomplete. Watson is reported back this week anyway.

items.h: Packers 45, Patriots 27
items.t: Jordan Love 372, three touchdowns, no interceptions, a 153.2 rating. Drake Maye threw three first-half picks.

items.h: Bengals 34, Falcons 17 in Madrid
items.t: Burrow 271 and three. JA'MARR CHASE 10 CATCHES FOR 155 - AND 142 OF THEM CAME IN THE FIRST 25 MINUTES.

items.h: The rest
items.t: Cowboys 27, Colts 23. Chiefs 35, Jets 12. Lions 19, Dolphins 9. Rams 20, Commanders 13. 49ers 38, Raiders 17. Seahawks 17, Cardinals 3.

items.h: Four for the record book
items.t: Brock Bowers set the record for MOST RECEPTIONS BY A TIGHT END THROUGH THREE SEASONS, 224. Christian McCaffrey's 37th career receiving touchdown passed Marshall Faulk for the most ever by a running back in the Super Bowl era. Jared Goff threw NO TOUCHDOWNS FOR THE FIRST TIME IN 30 STRAIGHT GAMES - in a game where BOTH PUNTERS COMPLETED FAKE-PUNT PASSES AND BOTH FINISHED WITH HIGHER PASSER RATINGS THAN THE STARTING QUARTERBACKS, 112.5 for Jack Fox and 118.8 for Bradley Pinion. And Denver's 16 is a league record.

items.h: Four byes - Chicago, Denver, Philadelphia and Tampa Bay
items.t: A 14-game week, 13 games left to play.

items.h: The top seeds
items.t: Buffalo 7-1 and San Francisco 7-1, with Denver 7-2 and Chicago 7-2 behind them.

items.h: The NFC North is four deep
items.t: Chicago 7-2 on bye, Detroit 6-2 in Munich, Minnesota 6-2 at Green Bay 6-3. Vikings-Packers is a swing game between two six-win teams, with a quarterback Minnesota acquired four days ago expected to start it.

items.h: The AFC North is a first-place game Sunday night
items.t: Pittsburgh and Cincinnati are both 6-2 on four-game winning streaks, and AP notes their combined .750 winning percentage is the highest for a Steelers-Bengals meeting this late since 2009. Baltimore is last in that division at 4-5 and has lost four straight.

items.h: The deadline passed Tuesday and 18 deals got done
items.t: The ones that matter this week: Kirk Cousins to Minnesota for a third, which made Fernando Mendoza the Raiders' quarterback. Josh Downs to Kansas City. Keenan Allen to San Francisco - and he may face a multi-game league suspension from an August DUI, unresolved. Jessie Bates III, Jordan Davis and Davon Godchaux to Jacksonville, which is why that defense is a top-four play. Brissett from Arizona to Baltimore.

items.h: Indianapolis kept Jonathan Taylor and sold everything around him
items.t: Nelson, Buckner, Allen, Downs and Pittman all went out the door. They kept the one player.

blocks.title: Block 3: Week 10 Picks, the Vegas Numbers and the Locks

items.h: 9:30 AM ET, and it kicks off during this show: Patriots at Lions in Munich, FOX
items.t: Allianz Arena. Detroit -2.5, total 49.5. This is also the ONLY game with official injury designations, because Munich files early - New England has Ben Brown, Carlton Davis III and TreVeyon Henderson OUT; Detroit has Kerby Joseph, Cade Mays and D.J. Reed OUT.

items.h: The 1:00 window
items.t: Chiefs at Falcons CBS, KC -3, 47.5. Texans at Browns FOX, HOU -4.5, 40.5. Vikings at Packers FOX, GB -3, 41.5. Dolphins at Colts CBS, IND -3.5, 38.5. Panthers at Saints FOX, NO -2.5, 48.5. Bills at Jets CBS, BUF -8.5, 50.5. Jaguars at Titans FOX, JAX -10.5, 46.5.

items.h: Late and primetime
items.t: Rams at Cardinals 4:05 CBS, LAR -9.5, 39.5. Seahawks at Raiders 4:05 CBS, SEA -6.5, 40.5 (BetMGM has this three points different). 49ers at Cowboys 4:25 FOX, SF -3.5, 55.5. Steelers at Bengals Sunday 8:20 NBC, CIN -3.5, 49.5. Chargers at Ravens Monday 8:15 ESPN, BAL -4.5, 38.5.

items.h: The line move of the week is not a spread, it is a total
items.t: CHARGERS-RAVENS OPENED AT 48.5 AND IS NOW 38.5 - a ten-point collapse, the biggest move on the board, on Lamar Jackson being out and an 0-8 offense that went 37 drives without a touchdown.

items.h: Two more big total moves, both quarterback injuries
items.t: Dolphins-Colts dropped nine points, 47.5 to 38.5, when Malik Willis went on IR. Rams-Cardinals dropped eight, 47.5 to 39.5, with Puka Nacua out, Davante Adams out and a rookie making his first NFL start.

items.h: On the spread side
items.t: Jacksonville moved from -2.5 to -10.5, eight points, and the 49ers-Cowboys line REVERSED from Dallas -1.5 to San Francisco -4.5.

items.h: Extremes
items.t: Biggest spread: Jacksonville -10.5. Highest total: 49ers-Cowboys at 55.5, the only game over 51. Lowest: Dolphins-Colts and Chargers-Ravens, both 38.5.

items.h: The thing to say out loud
items.t: Three of this week's four biggest market moves are quarterback injuries, and none of them are to teams anybody was watching in September.

segments.title: Topic 15. Sunday Night Football: Steelers at Bengals, 8:20 PM NBC

items.h: Outright first place in the AFC North
items.t: Cincinnati -3.5, total 49.5, at Paycor Stadium. Both 6-2, both on four-game streaks. Tirico, Collinsworth and Stark, with Football Night in America on site at 7:00.

items.h: Pittsburgh won the Week 3 meeting 30-27
items.t: A Chris Boswell walk-off field goal set up by a Derrick Harmon strip-sack. Burrow is 4-4 lifetime against Pittsburgh, and Rodgers outplayed him in that one.

items.h: Joe Burrow has four or more touchdowns in four straight games
items.t: He leads the NFL with 23 passing touchdowns and is second with 2,386 yards. Cincinnati is second in the league in scoring at 30 a game.

items.h: Aaron Rodgers makes his 44th Sunday Night Football appearance
items.t: The most of any active player, third all-time. T.J. Watt has 28 career multi-sack games, tied with Richard Dent for fifth-most by anybody in his first ten seasons. And NBC is on site for the first Steelers game since MIKE TOMLIN JOINED FOOTBALL NIGHT IN AMERICA.

items.h: Cincinnati's Thursday report - practice participation only, no designations
items.t: Jonathan Allen (rest) and Kyle Dugger (quad) did not practice either day; B.J. Hill limited Thursday; DJ Turner II and Dylan Fairchild full Thursday. THREE PLAYERS PRACTICED IN FULL OFF IR DESIGNATED-FOR-RETURN: Jalen Davis, Andrei Iosivas and Brian Parker II.

items.h: Pittsburgh's Thursday report
items.t: Cameron Heyward (rest) did not practice either day. T.J. WATT DID NOT PRACTICE WEDNESDAY AND WAS LIMITED THURSDAY. Darnell Washington and DeShon Elliott full Thursday; Derrick Harmon limited both days with his 21-day IR window opened Wednesday.

segments.title: Topic 16. Monday Night Football: Chargers at Ravens, 8:15 PM, ESPN

items.h: Two teams in trouble, and a total that fell ten points because of it
items.t: Baltimore -4.5, total 38.5, at M&T Bank Stadium. The 0-8 Chargers against a Baltimore team that has lost four straight and is last in the AFC North at 4-5.

items.h: Joe Buck and Troy Aikman, with a ManningCast on ESPN2
items.t: Lisa Salters and Laura Rutledge on the sidelines; Kevin Harlan and Kurt Warner on Westwood One. nfl.com lists ESPN only - see the verify list on the network.

items.h: Jacoby Brissett makes his first Ravens start
items.t: Lamar Jackson is out multiple weeks after thumb surgery and Tyler Huntley is on IR. Yahoo reports Jackson told teammates he intends to play again this season, but the timeline points to January - which means Baltimore has to still be alive for it to matter. Baltimore also goes to a different kicker, Riley Patterson.

items.h: Justin Herbert is NOT on the Chargers' injury report
items.t: A finger issue on the non-throwing hand that avoided real damage, and they have the extra day.

items.h: This is the weakest injury reporting on the board, so say so
items.t: nfl.com lists NO injuries at all for this game, which is a lag and not health. The Chargers' own Thursday report has NINE players who did not practice - Ladd McConkey (back), Khalil Mack (rest), Daiyan Henley (personal), Justin Eboigbe, Trey Pipkins III, Brandon Taylor, Brenen Thompson, Isas Waxter, Kendall Williamson - and nine more limited, including David Njoku, Tre' Harris and Denzel Perryman. NOT ONE CHARGER PRACTICED IN FULL.

items.h: Baltimore had nobody sit out
items.t: Jaylinn Hawkins, Olaivavega Ioane and Rashod Bateman limited Thursday. Monday teams file a day later than everybody else, so there will be no designations on this game until Saturday - do not say 'Out' or 'Questionable' on it today.

segments.title: Topic 17. The Vegas numbers - implied team totals

items.h: How these are built
items.t: Computed off the DraftKings board above, Friday Nov 13. Favorite is total plus spread over two; underdog is total minus spread over two. These are OUR numbers, not published figures, and the arithmetic has been checked twice.

items.h: The full board
items.t: Bills 29.5 / Jets 21.0. 49ers 29.5 / Cowboys 26.0. Jaguars 28.5 / Titans 18.0. Bengals 26.5 / Steelers 23.0. Lions 26.0 / Patriots 23.5. Saints 25.5 / Panthers 23.0. Chiefs 25.25 / Falcons 22.25. Rams 24.5 / Cardinals 15.0. Seahawks 23.5 / Raiders 17.0. Texans 22.5 / Browns 18.0. Packers 22.25 / Vikings 19.25. Ravens 21.5 / Chargers 17.0. Colts 21.0 / Dolphins 17.5.

items.h: Highest, and it is a tie - Buffalo and San Francisco at 29.5
items.t: And they get there completely differently. Buffalo is an 8.5-point favorite in a 50.5 against a 2-7 Jets team. San Francisco is only a 3.5-point favorite, but in a 55.5-point game, the highest total of the week by four. Then Jacksonville at 28.5.

items.h: The only game where both teams clear 23 is 49ers-Cowboys
items.t: 29.5 and 26.0. That is the start-both-sides game of the week and it is not close.

items.h: Lowest: Arizona at 15.0
items.t: The lowest implied total we have put on this board all season - lower than last week's Arizona number, which was also the lowest of the season. A rookie making his first NFL start, Michael Wilson out for the year, and the Rams on the other side. Then the Raiders and the Chargers tied at 17.0 and Miami at 17.5.

items.h: Three games to leave alone for skill-position starts
items.t: Dolphins-Colts at 38.5 with Miami at 17.5, Chargers-Ravens at 38.5 with the Chargers at 17.0, and Rams-Cardinals at 39.5 with Arizona at 15.0. In all three the market says use the defense, not the lineup - which is exactly why Indianapolis, Baltimore and the Rams are the three most recommended streams of the week.

items.h: One caution
items.t: The Seattle number assumes -6.5, and BetMGM has that game at -3.5. If Seattle is really -3.5, the Raiders come up a point and a half and Seattle comes down the same.

segments.title: Topic 18. Locks of the week and the close

items.h: One NFL play and one sentence from each panelist
items.t: Name the book and the number.

items.h: Close, beat one: the Munich kickoff is 9:30 in the morning, during this show
items.t: Anybody setting a lineup should have done it before they turned us on - and A.J. Brown's status was still a coin flip when this was written.

items.h: Beat two: four byes this week, a 14-game slate
items.t: Chicago, Denver, Philadelphia, Tampa Bay.

items.h: Beat three: next week is the heavy one - SIX teams on bye
items.t: Atlanta, Cleveland, Green Bay, the Rams, New England and Seattle. That hits almost every hot add on today's board, so if you spend on Kiner or Kaleb Johnson or Charbonnet today you need a Week 11 plan already. And Week 12 has no byes at all.

items.h: Tease next week
items.t: Whether West Virginia got to six, Houston coming to Morgantown, the third CFP rankings on Tuesday, and whether Philip Rivers was actually introduced at NC State.
